title: Horsford identity disambiguation and Pringle-network register
purpose: Track the identity of the Horsford associated with Gillett & Horsford / Southwick Nurseries while preventing publication-level over-merging with Frederick Hinsdale Horsford until an explicit firm-person source is recovered.

southwick_firm.direct_blaschka_link: Blaschka workshop letter of 19 July 1891 states that a California Fritillaria bulb had been sent the previous year by Gillett & Horsford, Southwick Mass.
southwick_firm.harvard_metadata: HOLLIS describes an 1891 folder as letters from Edward Gillett of Gillett and Horsford, plant nursery in Southwick, MA.
southwick_firm.primary_stationery: Pass 38 verifies repeated OCR of Southwick Nurseries (Gillett & Horsford) letterhead in the Edward Gillett-to-Watson block, including the printed cable address HORSFORD, SOUTHWICK.
southwick_firm.contemporary_1890_identity_bridge: The American Garden vol. XI (1890), article Some Native Orchids, ends 'Southwick, Mass. F. H. Horsford.' A later note identifies this piece as appearing in the April issue.

frederick_hinsdale_horsford_network.relation_to_southwick_firm: strongly_supported_same-person bridge via F. H. Horsford at Southwick in April 1890; exact partnership role still unresolved

documents.title: Some Native Orchids
documents.evidence: article ends 'Southwick, Mass. F. H. Horsford'; later note explicitly refers to the article as in the April issue
documents.research_value: direct contemporary geographic bridge between F. H. Horsford and Southwick during Gillett & Horsford's 1890 catalogue year

research_use: strong identity bridge to Southwick requiring explicit partnership closure

identity_hypothesis.hypothesis: Frederick Hinsdale Horsford was the Horsford associated with Gillett & Horsford, Southwick, Massachusetts
current_support: F. H. Horsford is directly placed at Southwick, Mass. in an April 1890 horticultural article
BHL independently identifies Frederick Hinsdale Horsford as a botanical correspondent to Sereno Watson repeatedly in 1890
Gillett & Horsford / Southwick Nurseries is independently attested in 1890 catalogue/publication metadata and 1891 Harvard archival description
Edward Gillett's surviving Southwick stationery uses cable address HORSFORD, SOUTHWICK
F. H. Horsford's native-orchid cultivation expertise matches the Southwick firm's native-plant commercial specialization
identity_hypothesis.remaining_gap: No inspected source yet explicitly says 'Frederick Hinsdale Horsford, partner in Gillett & Horsford' or equivalent.
identity_hypothesis.decision_rule: For discovery/search use likely_same_person. For publication-level actor merging, retain cross-referenced IDs until a contemporary catalogue, letterhead, directory, signature, advertisement or firm notice explicitly connects Frederick Hinsdale Horsford to Gillett & Horsford.

conceptual_note: If the identity is closed, the Southwick supplier node joins commercial nursery work, native-plant cultivation/field knowledge and Harvard taxonomic correspondence. Do not assume the Pringle relationship and Gillett relationship were mutually exclusive; overlapping associations remain possible.
